references.text: Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent by the oak at Zaanannim near Kedesh. This explains why Jael's tent was in this area.
Sisera is mentioned as the commander of King Jabin of Hazor, who had nine hundred iron chariots and oppressed Israel for twenty years.
Deborah's song describes how Jael, Heber's wife, killed Sisera in her tent, which is the direct continuation of this event.
Hobab, Moses' brother-in-law, was a Kenite. The Kenites had a friendly relationship with Israel, which explains why there was peace between Jabin and Heber's household.
Jabin, king of Hazor, is mentioned as one of the kings defeated by Joshua. This is the same royal dynasty that ruled over Hazor.
The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenites, went up from the City of Palms with the sons of Judah. This shows the connection between the Kenites and Israel.
